data.name: proposal
data.shape: { rebind: { agentId, agentName, fromStrategyName, toStrategyId, toStrategyName, toStrategyRevision, expectedRevision }, consequence, confirmationToken }
data.source: app.describeRebind.execute — the destination's name and revision come back from the platform, never from the URL

data.name: to
data.source: searchParams — the destination strategy id; all the query supplies

data.name: problem
data.source: searchParams — the reason the previous attempt was not performed. Two arms redirect here: destination-moved, and (since `the-outcome-reaches-the-person`) refused — BattleGrid's own refusal of the rebind, which used to escape as a thrown error and render a framework error page instead of a reason. A third failure shape, a lost account authority, deliberately does NOT arrive here; it travels as ?authority=

data.name: authority
data.source: searchParams — since `a-lost-authority-is-not-a-refusal`, the sentence a performRebind whose account authority is gone redirected back with (carrying ?to= as well, which the page then ignores). Read before anything else and, when present, it replaces the whole page with <AuthorityLost>.

components.purpose: Ask one question — replace this agent's configuration with another strategy's? — with the consequence stated as replacement, never merge.
components.current_implementation: max-w-2xl centered column, space-y-4, p-6. Branch order: not-connected, then authority-lost, then ?to=, then the describe. Without ?to= it renders 'Choose a strategy to rebind to', a sentence saying strategy browsing is not built yet, and — since `the-outcome-reaches-the-person` — a BUTTON_SECONDARY 'Back to the agent' anchor, so it is no longer a dead end. refused renders h1 'Cannot rebind' + the reason (role=alert, untinted text) and the same BUTTON_SECONDARY exit. All three describe-reaching branches mount `<CarriedProblem>` unconditionally — it renders null when there is no carried reason, so every `-with-problem` pairing above is a real rendering rather than a variant somebody has to remember. On refused two alerts stack — the carried reason for the click that bounced, then this page's own fresh failure. No roster read: the agent's name comes from the proposal, so there is no separate no-such-agent branch — an unknown agent surfaces as the describe's refusal. NEW since `a-lost-authority-is-not-a-refusal`: `authority-lost` is a fourth top-level branch, taken before ?to= is even looked at, that returns the shared `<AuthorityLost>` and nothing else — no proposal, no form, no exit link, and deliberately no CarriedProblem.
constraints: The page renders whole from one server round trip — no client JS, no hydration. A design requiring client-side interactivity changes behavior and is requires-spec-change.

The destination named in the consequence is read from the platform — openspec/specs/agent-authoring/spec.md:165-168 ('its name and its revision — never taken from the caller'). A design must not surface the URL's id as if it were the destination's identity.

Every describe-reaching branch renders the carried reason, not just the one that can offer a form — `tests/agent/refusals-reach-the-operator.test.ts` asserts one `<CarriedProblem>` per `<main>` in this file. A design that suppresses it on a terminal branch changes behavior and is requires-spec-change.
Where two alerts stack (carried reason above this page's own failure reason), both must stay readable as separate claims.
The exits on the no-destination and refused branches must stay visible targets, not prose links — they are the only way out of those branches.

The authority-lost branch renders no form, no carried problem and no exit, on purpose — 'a control that cannot work is not made honest by the sentence above it' (authority-lost.tsx). A design that gives this branch the confirmation or an exit back changes behavior and is requires-spec-change.

components.purpose: Show why the previous attempt was not performed — the destination moved, or BattleGrid refused it — above whatever this request could compose.
components.current_implementation: The shared `CarriedProblem` component (src/presentation/components/carried-problem.tsx), extracted by `the-outcome-reaches-the-person` from the ternary that used to be inline on this page. Carries DT-0004's danger treatment unchanged — rounded-gc-2 border border-danger-default bg-danger-subtle p-4 text-sm text-text-primary with role=alert, opening with a semibold 'Refused: ' prefix so the state is named as well as tinted — and returns null when `problem` is undefined, which is what lets every branch mount it unconditionally. Two arms now feed it: destination-moved and the command's new refused arm.
constraints: role=alert must survive.

The pairing is spec: the fresh proposal and the reason it was needed arrive together — openspec/specs/agent-authoring/spec.md:189-194 ('the user is told the destination changed while they were reading, and is offered a fresh proposal'). The banner must stay adjacent to the re-described proposal, not become a toast or a separate page.
The reason is platform-authored and unbounded — the block must wrap rather than clip, and must not truncate or paraphrase.

Shared by eleven pages now (agent deploy/undeploy/rebind/archive/reactivate, strategy archive/restore/fork, both /pending surfaces, recorder trim) — restyle it in the component, never per page. `tests/agent/refusals-reach-the-operator.test.ts` fails any file that hand-rolls it again.
Rendering nothing when there is no problem is load-bearing — a design must not give it a reserved empty slot or a placeholder.
The 'Refused: ' prefix is part of the treatment — a design may restyle the prefix but must not drop the naming of the state.

components.purpose: The confirmation for the most destructive thing this product can do: one committing button, one visible way out, and the consequence read first.

actions.effect: POSTs the server action with agentId, confirmationToken, toStrategyId, toStrategyRevision, expectedRevision; success lands on /agents/[id]; a moved destination or a platform refusal both redirect back here with ?to= and ?problem=; a lost account authority redirects back with ?to= and ?authority= instead, which renders the page as AuthorityLost with no form

components.current_implementation: Shared RebindConfirm (rebind-confirm.tsx): space-y-4 form, h2 'Rebind <agent> to <strategy>?', the consequence block, five hidden inputs carrying the confirmation binding, then the buttons in flex flex-col gap-3 tablet:flex-row tablet:flex-wrap. DT-0018 has landed: the row stacks full-width below the `tablet` breakpoint and only becomes a wrapping row above it. The missing `agentId` hidden input — the behavior gap this manifest recorded last time, which made every submit throw `FormError: agentId is required` and render a framework error page — is fixed: the field is now rendered, with a comment naming the failure.
constraints: The hidden binding (agent, destination, destination revision) is the confirmation ceremony — openspec/specs/agent-authoring/spec.md:166-168 ('the confirmation SHALL be bound to the agent, the destination, and the destination's revision as described'). The form must keep exactly one submit path.
Cancel must remain a visible peer of the submit, never a text link beneath it (DT-0002 ruling, restated in control.ts).

The stacking breakpoint is `tablet`; both controls carry `w-full tablet:w-auto` so the commit and its peer are the same width when stacked. A design must not restore a wrapping row at mobile width — this button's label is the longest in the product ('Replace <agent>'s configuration with <strategy>'s'), so it wraps to several lines and a peer beside it is unreadable narrow.
Adding or removing a hidden field is behavior, not presentation — requires-spec-change.

components.purpose: State that rebinding replaces the agent's inherited configuration in full — replacement, never merge — before the button that does it.
components.current_implementation: role=alert div, rounded-gc-2 border border-consequence-border bg-consequence-subtle p-4 text-sm text-text-primary. DT-0018 has landed: the anonymous border-border-default this was built with is gone and the block now wears the house consequence role. Two paragraphs, unchanged: a font-medium lead 'This replaces configuration. It is not a merge.' then the platform-derived consequence sentence.
constraints: The replacement framing is spec — openspec/specs/agent-authoring/spec.md:162-165 ('MUST state that the agent's inherited configuration will be replaced in full, and MUST NOT describe it as a change of strategy alone') and :171-174. The lead sentence must not be softened or dropped.
The consequence text is the same string the token was issued against and stored with — a design must not paraphrase, truncate, or summarize it.
Consequence outranks everything on a screen (system.json principle) — this block must not become lighter than the buttons below it.
role=alert must survive.

When a bounce carried a problem, the danger-tinted banner sits directly above this consequence-tinted block — since DT-0018 both are tinted, so the two roles must stay separable at a glance; 'notice never borrows danger's colour' (system.json principle) binds the pair.

components.purpose: Commit the rebind, named so it agrees to something in particular: 'Replace <agent>'s configuration with <strategy>'s'.
components.current_implementation: BUTTON_PRIMARY constant from control.ts — accent.default bg, min-h-control (44px, DT-0003's token), rounded-gc-2, hover to accent.hover over duration-fast, active holds hover at duration-instant. Since DT-0018 it carries `w-full tablet:w-auto`, so it fills the stacked row on mobile. No pending/loading state between click and redirect. system.json declares this primitive with states [default, hover, active, focused, disabled, loading]; `disabled` and `loading` are declared there as names with no treatment and are implemented by nothing in control.ts, so no form in the product can reach them (#153). The harness half of that is now solved — tests/rendering/support/form-status.ts reaches both states — so what is missing is the look, which is this round's to decide. DT-0022 added the primitive's `disabled` treatment to this constant — bg.sunken ground, text.disabled label, border.subtle edge and cursor not-allowed, stated rather than an opacity. DT-0022 defined the primitive's `disabled` treatment on this constant, but **nothing in the product enters it** — so it is not listed as a state of this surface. system.json declares it and DT-0022 styles it; a surface claiming a state it cannot reach is the same fiction DT-0003 refused for the ghost and danger variants.
constraints: Deliberately NOT danger-styled — DT-0002's ruling, restated both in control.ts and in rebind-confirm.tsx's own comment: the weight is on the consequence above, and a hazard-coloured control trains a flinch at the action the page exists to offer.
The label names the operation and both parties — 'OK' or 'Confirm' would be a button that agrees to nothing in particular. Copy changes here are behavior.
Styling changes go through the BUTTON_PRIMARY constant in control.ts.
44px minimum tap target (system.json principle).
Focus ring comes from the one global rule in globals.css — do not add a per-element ring.

components.purpose: Every way out of this route: 'Keep it bound to <current strategy>' beside the commit, and 'Back to the agent' on the no-destination and refused branches.
components.current_implementation:
An anchor wearing BUTTON_SECONDARY — inline-flex centering, min-h-control, DT-0004's hover (border-strong + bg-sunken over duration-fast). Worn in three places since `the-outcome-reaches-the-person`: the cancel inside RebindConfirm, and the exits the no-destination and refused branches gained. The cancel additionally carries `w-full tablet:w-auto` since DT-0018; the two branch exits were untouched by that ticket and still sit inside a text-sm

, so each is a 44px box in a prose paragraph. Where this is an anchor it can never be pending — it submits nothing. Where a surface uses it as a GET submit (the deploy chooser's ask), it can, and system.json's declared `disabled` and `loading` states are unimplemented there too (#153). Recorded on button-primary rather than here, because that is the control a perform runs through.
constraints: Must remain an anchor (pure navigation, no form participation) and a visible peer of the submit.
Styling changes go through the BUTTON_SECONDARY constant in control.ts.
44px minimum tap target (system.json principle).
The no-destination and refused branches have no other exit — a design must not demote these to prose links.

components.purpose: Say that the account's BattleGrid authority is gone — not that this rebind was refused — where the operator was standing when their submit failed.

actions.effect: Anchor to /connect, where a new grant is obtained. Rendered only on remedy-reconnect. It navigates and submits nothing, and it is not the operation that failed — that control stays absent on both branches.

components.current_implementation:
Shared `AuthorityLost` component (src/presentation/components/authority-lost.tsx), also mounted by the agent deploy, undeploy and rebind pages and the strategy rule editor. It replaces the whole page rather than banding the top of one: its own `
`, h1 'Your BattleGrid authority is no longer valid' in text-text-primary, the carried sentence in `rounded-gc-2 border border-danger-default bg-danger-subtle p-4 text-sm text-text-primary` with role=alert — the same treatment CarriedProblem wears — then a text-sm text-text-secondary paragraph: 'Nothing was changed. Until this is fixed, no operation on this account can succeed — including the one you just tried.' **Since `a-remedy-is-a-target-not-a-sentence` (#182) it also takes the deployment's `remedy` and branches on it.** On `reconnect` it appends a `

` holding a BUTTON_SECONDARY anchor to /connect reading 'Connect your BattleGrid account again'. On `repair-the-key` it appends nothing, because replacing an environment variable and restarting a process is not something a link can do. The remedy value is fixed once at src/composition.ts (`config.personal ? 'repair-the-key' : 'reconnect'`) and passed down, so the component never works out which deployment it is on. Nothing has designed any of this; it was built wearing existing tokens, and the anchor reuses the primitive NotConnected already uses for the same purpose rather than introducing a treatment.
constraints: It renders instead of the ceremony, not above it — a design must not turn this into a banner over the proposal. The reason the page has no form is that no call on this account can succeed.

The sentence is passed in and printed verbatim, remedy included — a design must not template it or prefix it. The remedy is **also offered as a target where the deployment has one**: the component links to /connect on `remedy-reconnect` and draws nothing on `remedy-repair-the-key`. A design must not draw that link unconditionally — that is how a personal deployment gets told to press a connect button it does not have — and must not remove it from the reconnect branch, where DT-0006's ruling holds: a remedy is a target, not a sentence.

The two branches are one component and one treatment. The difference between them is whether the anchor renders, not how the page looks. A design that gave the two deployments different layouts would be designing for a distinction the operator can neither see nor change.

It must stay visually distinct from CarriedProblem even though both currently wear danger: one says this attempt was refused and something else may work, the other says nothing will. If a design keeps them identical it should say that is a decision.
role=alert must survive on the reason.
Shared with agent deploy, agent undeploy and the strategy rule editor — restyle it in the component, never per page.

components.purpose: Turn away a request without authority, with the one remedy that works: connect.
components.current_implementation: Shared NotConnected component (require-connection.tsx): h1 + message, and since DT-0006 the connect link is an anchor wearing BUTTON_SECONDARY — the way in as a target, not a sentence, at the 44px floor with secondary's hover. Used by every authenticated page, so this treatment is inherited everywhere. This is the one branch that does not mount CarriedProblem — it renders before searchParams are read.
constraints: Every no-authority cause renders this same page by design (see design W-C) — a design must not invent per-cause variants.

flows.name: Rebind an agent
steps: arrive carrying ?to=<strategyId>
read that this replaces, not merges, in the platform-derived sentence
submit 'Replace <agent>'s configuration with <strategy>'s'
land on /agents/[id] rebound

flows.name: The destination moved while reading
steps: submit
the fresh read finds a different revision (or cannot read the destination)
nothing is attempted; redirected back here with ?to= and ?problem=
the problem banner (shared CarriedProblem) states the reason above a freshly described proposal

flows.name: BattleGrid refuses the rebind itself
steps: submit
the platform rejects it — revision moved underneath, not permitted (CONFLICT, live-confirmed 2026-08-12)
the command's refused arm returns the reason instead of letting it escape as a thrown error
redirected back here with ?to= and ?problem=; the banner states the reason above the fresh proposal, or above 'Cannot rebind' if the re-describe fails too

flows.name: The account's authority is gone
steps: submit 'Replace <agent>'s configuration with <strategy>'s'
the platform answers that the connection or credential is no longer valid
performRebind's authority-lost arm — checked before destination-moved and refused — redirects back here with ?to= and ?authority=

the page renders <AuthorityLost> alone and ignores the ?to=: the reason, and that nothing was changed and nothing on this account can succeed until it is fixed. No form to retry with, and no exit link.

flows.name: No proposal can be made
steps: the describe refuses (not rebindable, a no-op, destination unavailable)
'Cannot rebind' states the reason; no token is minted
'Back to the agent' is the way out

flows.name: Walk away
steps: click 'Keep it bound to <current strategy>'
back on /agents/[id], nothing changed

accessibility.notes: The carried problem, consequence, refusal and authority-lost messages all carry role=alert; on a bounced branch two of them are adjacent. The authority-lost branch has an alert and no focusable element at all — it is the one state on this surface with nothing to tab to. Focus ring is global (focus-visible, 2px). No client JS: every state change is a full navigation.
